subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs treat `deleteAfterRun` as per-run session cleanup, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain one-shot-only for all cron jobs?
rationale: Current code has evidence for both directions: the linked bug needs recurring isolated session cleanup, while docs/plugin scheduling and a competing PR frame `deleteAfterRun` as one-shot-only.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-job upgrade or doctor coverage, docs/API alignment, and reconciliation with the competing one-shot-only PR.

options.title: Enforce one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after it covers Gateway/UI callers and legacy recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Allow this PR to affect only newly normalized jobs and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-job upgrade or doctor coverage, docs/API alignment, and reconciliation with the competing one-shot-only PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership signal across cron normalization, SQLite persistence, and service-job lifecycle surfaces.
